I'll run the alchemy skill as requested.

**Dispatch:** `DIRECT → M` — "speculative abstraction, worth question" maps to exactly one gate. Companions: none triggered yet (no dependency, data-shape, doc-location, or observability signal in the subject).

**What I found.** There's no CLI code in this working directory — only the skill library — so everything below is scored from your description, not from your repo. The proposal splits into two candidates, and they get different answers. The plugin system itself: don't build it, and record why so it isn't re-proposed without new evidence (the record calls this DROP). The thing that decided it is that a plugin extension point's prerequisites don't hold — there is one implementation, no second one named, and no requester — so it fails the optionality test outright (§8a: speculative optionality loses to YAGNI). Compounding it: a JSON-on-stdout CLI already composes with `jq`, `mlr`, `yq`, and `csvkit`, so irreplaceability (`I`) is near zero, and a zero on any value axis zeroes ordinary product value. The second candidate, *supporting some future second format*, is a real possibility with no evidence yet: hold it with a trigger (the record calls this DEFER).

**Why it matters.** Acting means shipping a discovery/registry/loader layer plus a public interface third parties write against — that is a one-way door under the irreversibility tax (§8b), which *raises* the value bar exactly where value is lowest, and removal in 12 months would cost more than building it today. Not acting costs you roughly a day whenever format #2 is actually requested: a `--format` flag and one formatter function. The asymmetry is large and points one way. What this evidence does *not* reach: whether you have a partner or roadmap commitment I can't see — one named, probable consumer of a second format changes the DEFER, though it still wouldn't justify a *plugin* system over a `--format` switch.

**Do this first.**
1. Write the rejection down where it will be found — a one-line ADR or issue: "No plugin system; no second output format has been requested. Revisit on first concrete request." That is the artifact that stops re-litigation.
2. Free and worth doing regardless: keep serialization out of computation, so the command computes a plain data structure and one call turns it into JSON. That is `architecture-guidelines` conformance, not an abstraction, and it is what makes format #2 cheap.
3. Answer one question for yourself: can you name the second format *and* who asked for it? If yes, that changes the DEFER, not the DROP.

**What I did not check.** Your actual CLI — I had no repo access, so the cost figures below are estimates, not measurements; `rg -n "json" --type <lang>` over your CLI's output path closes it. Structural complexity was not measured by the C gate (`structural-simplification` was not run): there is no code or diff to measure, and a prospective delta on an unseen codebase would be invented. Whether a contract or compliance obligation mandates a specific format (§8c floor) — I have no source for that; check your customer agreements.
